transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess what finally brought me in is… I don’t feel like myself. The part of me that used to reach out to people, or enjoy my work, or want to go to yoga or galleries, even just sit and journal—that all feels like it’s gone very quiet.

I’m still doing what I have to do, mostly, but it feels more like I’m just moving through obligations than actually living in any of it.
How long have you been feeling this way?
It’s been about eight months, I’d say. It started around when we took my older relative into our apartment, and since then the way I think, work, and connect with people has just felt different.
Do you still find pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy?

Not really, no. I still do some of the things I used to, but they don’t feel the same. Work, yoga, going to galleries, even journaling… they used to give me something, or help me feel connected. Now it’s more like I’m just getting through what I’m supposed to do. The enjoyment feels muted, I guess.
Have you been having any thoughts about death, or wishing you weren't alive?
No… I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve felt really flat and disconnected, but I haven’t been wishing I wasn’t alive, and I haven’t had thoughts about hurting myself.
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge more often than usual?
I’m not sure. I wouldn’t say I feel anxious exactly, or more on edge than usual. I’ve felt off, but not in a nervous or panicky way.
Have you been feeling more tired than usual?
I haven’t really noticed being more tired than usual. My energy isn’t great, but I can’t say it’s clearly worse or that I’m exhausted all the time.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight recently?
No, I haven’t really noticed any change in my weight. My clothes seem to fit about the same.
Do you feel like you're moving or reacting more slowly than you used to?
I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed myself moving slower or taking longer to react than I used to.
Have you been feeling worthless or guilty about things?
Not really. I mean, I get frustrated with myself sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling worthless or especially guilty about things.
Have you been feeling sad most of the time?
I wouldn’t say I’ve been sad most of the time. I have some down moments, but it’s not like I’m feeling sad all day or most days.
Are there any activities that you still enjoy or find pleasure in?

I can still do things, but I don’t really enjoy them the way I used to. Work, yoga, going to galleries, even journaling… they all used to feel meaningful or at least satisfying. Lately it’s more like I’m just getting through what I’m supposed to do. The part of me that reaches for people or gets pleasure from things feels kind of quiet.
Do you think people have noticed a change in the way you move or carry yourself?

Yes, I think so. A few times in team meetings, or even with clients, I’ve caught myself arranging pens in these exact little patterns, or repeating a phrase someone just said before I can stop myself. And then people look at me like I’ve kind of… stepped outside the room for a second.
Do you feel like your thoughts are slower than they used to be?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed my thoughts being slower exactly. Sometimes I pause or lose track a little, but I wouldn’t say I feel slowed down in my thinking.
Have you experienced any unusual or strange perceptions, like hearing voices or seeing things that others can't?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t heard voices or seen things that other people couldn’t see. At least, nothing like that that I’m aware of.
Have you noticed yourself fidgeting or having trouble sitting still more often than usual?

Not really fidgeting, exactly. It’s more like I’ll get focused on small things with my hands, like arranging pens into a certain pattern during a meeting, or I’ll repeat something someone just said before I even realize I’m doing it. It’s happened a few times, and people seem to notice.
Do you feel like you're unable to react to normally pleasurable events or activities, even when good things happen to you?

Yes. That’s actually a big part of why I came in. Things I used to really enjoy—my work, yoga, going to galleries, even journaling—just don’t feel like they reach me the same way now. I still do some of them, or at least go through the motions, but it feels more like I’m just getting through obligations than actually taking pleasure in them. And I’m not reaching out to people the way I used to.
Do you feel like you've been restless or have an inability to sit still?

Not in the sense of pacing or feeling like I can’t stay seated. It’s more that, a few times in meetings or even with clients, I’ve caught myself arranging pens into very specific patterns, or repeating a phrase someone just said before I can stop myself. And then people look at me like I’ve sort of checked out for a moment.
Have you felt like you're moving or acting more impulsively than you used to?

Maybe a little, but not like doing risky things suddenly. It’s more these small actions that happen before I really think about them. In meetings, or even with clients, I’ve caught myself arranging pens into exact patterns, or repeating a phrase someone just said before I can stop myself. Then people look at me like I’ve sort of… stepped outside the room for a second.
Do you feel like your body movements or physical activity have changed in any way since you started feeling this way?

Yes, a little. Not like big movements or anything, but I’ve noticed these odd things I do without meaning to. Like in team meetings, or even with clients, I’ll start arranging pens into exact patterns, or I’ll repeat a phrase someone just said before I can stop myself. It’s happened enough that people look at me like I’ve kind of stepped out of the room for a moment.
Do you feel like there's been a noticeable change in how actively you're engaging with your environment or the people around you, either more or less than before?

Yes, less than before. I’m still doing what I have to do, but it feels more like I’m just moving through obligations. The part of me that used to reach out to people, or enjoy my work, yoga, galleries, even journaling… it’s gone very quiet. I don’t feel as connected to any of it.
